title.title: The Turing degrees have no nontrivial symmetry
title.subtitle: Claim: every automorphism of the Turing degrees, ordered by $\le_T$, is the identity

beats.text: Schematic: Turing degrees, ordered by 'computable from'; $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are incomparable
Slaman–Woodin: an automorphism fixes every degree above $\mathbf{0}''$ (filled)
The claim: it fixes every degree, so the identity is the only one

sources.quote: Every order automorphism of the partial order of all Turing degrees (degrees of subsets of N under Turing reducibility) is the identity, in ZFC
Slaman-Woodin: every automorphism is the identity above 0'' and Aut(D) is countable

The paper itself is only 10 pages because it takes as an external input the Slaman-Woodin theorem that every automorphism is induced by an arithmetic (Borel) function on reals, cited from an unpublished 2005 manuscript.

steps: Any symmetry comes from an explicit map on reals
Feed it four mixes of a real $t$ and two generic reals
The four outputs give back $t$, so nothing can move

data.result: $t$ recovered: the symmetry is the identity
